mainTopic: Prophets and their punishments, אגדות about the עקידה, and how a נביא שהדיח and מדיחי עיר הנדחת are put to death
overview: This amud finishes the list of people who die at the hands of Heaven. The friend of מיכה ignored a prophet, and עדו הנביא broke his own prophecy; both were killed by a lion. A ברייתא says one who holds back his prophecy gets lashes. אביי explains that his fellow prophets know the prophecy and can warn him, and the גמרא defends this using the case of יונה. Next the גמרא asks how a listener knows to obey a prophet. The answer is that the prophet gives a sign, unless he is already known as a true prophet, as with אברהם at הר המוריה and אליהו at הר הכרמל. This leads into stories about the עקידה: why ה׳ tested אברהם, why He said 'please', and how אברהם turned away the שטן on the road. Finally, a ברייתא brings a מחלוקת between the חכמים and רבי שמעון about whether a נביא שהדיח and the מדיחי עיר הנדחת get סקילה or חנק, along with the sources each side uses. A new teaching of רב חסדא begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The friend of מיכה ignored a prophet and was punished
steps.stepSummary: The example of someone who ignores a prophet's words is the friend of מיכה, who refused to strike him when told to by ה׳'s word and was killed by a lion.
steps.simpleTranslation: An example is the friend of מיכה. The פסוק says: 'A man from the sons of the prophets told his friend, by ה׳'s word: Please hit me. The man refused to hit him.' Another פסוק says: 'He told him: Because you did not listen...' and a lion killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an example for the משנה's case of someone who ignores a prophet's words (המוותר על דברי נביא). It brings two פסוקים to show the crime and the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows the sin: a prophet asked, by ה׳'s word, to be struck, and his friend refused. The second פסוק shows the punishment: because he did not listen, a lion killed him. That is death at the hands of Heaven, just as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: Disciples of the prophets, a group of prophets

phrases.english: The colleague of מיכה,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is finishing an example started just before this: someone who ignored a prophet's words.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And a certain man of the sons of the prophets
phrases.notes: מלכים א 20:35

phrases.english: said to his colleague by the word of ה׳:
Strike me, please.
And the man refused to strike him.'
And it is written: 'Then he said to him:
Because you have not listened, etc.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 20:36. The 'etc.' points to the rest of the פסוק, where a lion kills him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the example for המוותר על דברי נביא, which began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ignoring a prophet's command is punished by death at the hands of Heaven, as happened to the friend of מיכה.

steps.title: עדו הנביא broke his own prophecy
steps.stepSummary: The example of a prophet who breaks his own prophecy is עדו הנביא. He was told not to eat in בית אל, ate anyway after another prophet persuaded him, and was killed by a lion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה's case of 'a prophet who broke his own words' is like עדו הנביא. He said: 'This is what I was commanded.' The other prophet said: 'I am also a prophet like you.' Then: 'He went back with him.' And then: 'He went, and a lion found him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, a prophet who disobeys his own prophecy, and gives עדו הנביא as an example. Four פסוקים show the whole story step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First פסוק‎: ה׳ commanded him not to eat or drink there. Second: another man claimed to be a prophet too and told him to come eat. Third: he went back and ate, going against his own prophecy. Fourth: a lion killed him, which is death at the hands of Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: A prophet who disobeyed his own prophecy
And he went back with him

steps.whatToRemember: Both examples so far end the same way: a lion kills the person. That is how the פסוקים show death at the hands of Heaven.

phrases.english: And a prophet who violated his own words:
for example, עדו the prophet,
as it is written: 'For so it was commanded me',
phrases.notes: מלכים א 13:9. He was told not to eat or drink in that place.

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And he said to him:
I too am a prophet like you',
phrases.notes: מלכים א 13:18

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And he went back with him',
and it is written: 'And he went, and a lion found him.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 13:24

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנָבִיא שֶׁעָבַר עַל דִּבְרֵי עַצְמוֹ: כְּגוֹן עִדּוֹ הַנָּבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A prophet who disobeys his own prophecy dies at the hands of Heaven, as happened to עדו.

steps.title: A ברייתא: one who holds back his prophecy gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recited before רב חסדא a teaching that a prophet who holds back his prophecy is punished with lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught in front of רב חסדא: Someone who holds back his prophecy gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A ברייתא is quoted that says a prophet who keeps his prophecy to himself gets lashes (מלקות).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says this sin brings death at the hands of Heaven. The ברייתא adds that there is also a human punishment, lashes. This sets up רב חסדא's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter of ברייתות taught before him
One who holds back (suppresses) his prophecy

phrases.english: A tanna taught before רב חסדא:
One who suppresses his prophecy is flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about הכובש את נבואתו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who holds back his prophecy gets lashes.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks: who could warn him?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא compares it to eating wormy dates hidden in a sieve. Nobody can see the sin, so nobody can give the warning that lashes require.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: Does someone who eats dates in a sieve get lashes? Who warns him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges the ברייתא. Lashes need a warning before the sin, and nobody knows that the prophet received a prophecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can only get lashes if witnesses warned him first (התראה). Someone eating wormy dates inside a sieve cannot be seen, so nobody can warn him. In the same way, a prophecy is hidden inside the prophet, so how could anyone warn him?

keyTerms.meaning: Warns (gives the required warning before punishment)

phrases.english: He said to him: Is one who eats dates
in a sieve flogged?
phrases.notes: The dates may have worms, but they are hidden in the sieve, so no one sees what he eats.

phrases.english: Who forewarns him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: מַאן דְּאָכֵיל תַּמְרֵי בְּאַרְבְּלָא לָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that הכובש את נבואתו gets lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lashes require התראה, but nobody knows about a hidden prophecy, so nobody can give the warning.

steps.title: אביי: his fellow prophets warn him
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that other prophets can warn him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: His fellow prophets warn him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the ברייתא. Other prophets can know about the prophecy, so they can be the ones who warn him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that nobody knew. אביי says some people do know: the other prophets. That makes a proper warning possible, so lashes can be given.

phrases.english: אביי said: His fellow prophets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies who can give the warning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nobody knows about the prophecy, so no warning is possible
steps.terutzMaskana: Fellow prophets know about it and can warn him

steps.title: How do the other prophets know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the fellow prophets would know about his prophecy.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do they know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question on אביי's answer: how would other prophets know what was revealed to him? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer only works if the other prophets really know about the prophecy. So the גמרא wants the source for that knowledge.

phrases.english: From where do they know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of אביי's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the fellow prophets know about another prophet's prophecy

steps.title: ה׳ reveals His plans to the prophets
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a פסוק in עמוס‎: ה׳ does nothing without revealing His secret to His prophets.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because it is written: 'For ה׳ אלקים will do nothing unless He has revealed His secret' to His servants the prophets.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with a פסוק‎: ה׳ tells His plans to the prophets. So the other prophets also know about the message.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ה׳ shares His plans with His prophets in general, the other prophets know what message was given. That knowledge lets them warn the prophet who holds it back.

phrases.english: אביי said: As it is written:
'For ה׳ [Elokim] will do nothing
phrases.notes: עמוס 3:7. The word in square brackets is added so the line matches the wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: unless He reveals His secret.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: דִּכְתִיב כִּי לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ reveals His plans to all His prophets, as the פסוק in עמוס says

steps.title: Maybe Heaven changed its mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe Heaven took back the prophecy, so the prophet is no longer required to say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they changed their mind about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the other prophets can warn him. Maybe Heaven canceled the message, and he is right to stay quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the other prophets heard the original prophecy, they cannot be sure it still stands. If Heaven took it back, the prophet would not be sinning by keeping silent, and their warning would be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: They changed their mind about it

phrases.english: And perhaps they reconsidered regarding it?
phrases.notes: 'They' means Heaven, which may have taken back the prophecy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that fellow prophets can surely know the prophet must speak
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The prophecy might have been canceled, so the other prophets cannot be sure he is sinning.

steps.title: If it were canceled, all prophets would be told
steps.stepSummary: If Heaven had taken back the prophecy, all the prophets would have been told about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were true that they changed their mind, they would have informed all the prophets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A change would also be revealed to all the prophets, so they would know it had been canceled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the original message reaches all the prophets, a cancellation would reach them too. So if they heard no cancellation, they know the prophecy still stands and can warn him. This keeps the ברייתא's ruling of lashes in place.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא stands: one who holds back his prophecy can get lashes, because the other prophets know about the prophecy and would also know if it were canceled, so they can warn him.

phrases.english: If it were so that they reconsidered regarding it,
they would certainly have informed
all the prophets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אִיתָא דְּהָדְרִי בֵּיהּ, אוֹדוֹעֵי הֲווֹ מוֹדְעִי לְכֻלְּהוּ נְבִיאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extends the same rule: changes are revealed to all prophets too
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prophecy may have been secretly canceled
steps.terutzMaskana: A cancellation would be told to all prophets, so with no notice they know it still stands

steps.title: What about יונה, who was not told the prophecy was canceled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer using יונה: Heaven canceled the destruction of נינוה, but יונה was not told.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at יונה: Heaven changed its mind about destroying נינוה and did not tell him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks Step 9, which said all the prophets are always told when Heaven takes back a prophecy. It points to יונה as a case where this did not happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 claimed a canceled prophecy is always made known to the prophets. נינוה repented and was saved, yet יונה seems not to have been told. That looks like a case that breaks the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at... (opens a challenge from a known case)
They went back on it, changed their mind

phrases.english: But there is Jonah,
where they changed their mind and did not inform him?
phrases.notes: "They" means Heaven. נינוה repented, so the destruction was called off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in Step 9 that a canceled prophecy is always revealed to the prophets.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that if Heaven takes back a prophecy, all prophets are informed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counter-example: נינוה was spared, and יונה was apparently not told.

steps.title: יונה's prophecy was never canceled; it had two meanings
steps.stepSummary: יונה was told 'נינוה will be overturned,' which could mean destroyed or turned to good. So nothing was canceled.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the start יונה was told to say 'נינוה will be overturned.' He did not know if that meant for good or for bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the prophecy about נינוה was never taken back at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'overturned' could mean the city would be destroyed, or that the people would turn their lives around. When נינוה repented, the prophecy came true in the good sense. So there was no cancellation that the prophets needed to hear about.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the prophecy failed. The גמרא's point is that it came true, just in the good meaning of 'overturned.'

phrases.english: Jonah, from the start,
they told him: "Nineveh will be overturned."
phrases.notes: יונה 3:4

phrases.english: He did not know
whether it was for good or for bad.
phrases.notes: "Overturned" for good means the people turning away from their bad ways.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the יונה challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the prophecy: it was never canceled because it had two possible meanings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נינוה's survival means Heaven canceled the prophecy without telling יונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prophecy was fulfilled in its good meaning, so there was no cancellation to report.

steps.title: How does someone know he will be punished for ignoring a prophet?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the person who ignores a נביא: how can he know this is a real נביא, so that he deserves punishment?
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who ignores a prophet's words: how does he know he will be punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another person on the list of those punished: someone who ignores a נביא. It asks how he could know the speaker is a true נביא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Punishing someone only makes sense if he could have known the message truly came from ה׳. Anyone can claim to be a prophet, so the גמרא asks what tells the listener to take this one seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives up on, ignores

phrases.english: One who ignores the words of a prophet,
how does he know that he will be punished?
phrases.notes: He means: how could he know this man is really a prophet he must obey?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְוַותֵּר עַל דִּבְרֵי נָבִיא, מְנָא יָדַע דְּאִיעֲנַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the prophet who holds back his prophecy to the listener who ignores a prophet.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the listener can know the speaker is a true prophet, so that punishing him is fair.

steps.title: The prophet gave him a sign
steps.stepSummary: He is punished only when the נביא gave him an אות proving he is a prophet.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the prophet gave him a sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the listener knows because the נביא showed him an אות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sign proves the speaker is a real נביא. Once the listener has seen it, he has no excuse for ignoring the message, so he can be punished.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign that proves someone is a prophet

phrases.english: It is where he gave him a sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The listener is punished when the prophet proved himself with a sign.

steps.title: But מיכה gave no sign, and the man was still punished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: in the story of מיכה, no אות was given, yet the man who ignored him was punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at מיכה: he did not give a sign, and still the man was punished!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 13 with the case of מיכה, where there was no sign but there was punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If punishment requires a sign, the man who ignored מיכה should not have been punished. Since he was punished without any sign, the rule from Step 13 seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The prophet whose friend refused his request and was punished

phrases.english: But there is Micah,
phrases.notes: This is the story in מלכים א 20:35-36: the man who refused the prophet's request was killed by a lion.

phrases.english: who did not give him a sign,
and he was punished?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִיכָה, דְּלָא יְהַב לֵיהּ אוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a listener is punished only if the prophet gave a sign.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counter-example: מיכה gave no sign, yet the listener was punished.

steps.title: An established prophet is different
steps.stepSummary: A נביא who is already מוחזק (known as a true prophet) does not need a sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he is already established as a prophet, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: מיכה was already known as a true נביא, so no sign was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign is needed only for an unknown prophet. Once someone is known as a true prophet, people must listen to him without a new sign. So the punishment in the מיכה story makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Established, already known (here, as a true prophet)

phrases.english: Where he is established, it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מיכה challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a sign is needed only for a prophet who is not yet established.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every prophet needs a sign before a listener can be punished.
steps.terutzMaskana: A prophet already known as true (מוחזק) needs no sign.

steps.title: Proof from אברהם and אליהו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that an established נביא needs no sign: יצחק obeyed אברהם at הר המוריה, and the people followed אליהו at הר הכרמל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you do not say this, how did יצחק listen to אברהם at הר המוריה? And how did the people rely on אליהו at הר הכרמל and bring an offering outside the בית המקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two stories to support Step 15. In both, people obeyed a prophet without a sign, even when it meant doing something extreme.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יצחק let himself be offered as a קרבן, and the people did שחוטי חוץ, which is normally forbidden. They could only have done this because אברהם and אליהו were already known as true prophets. This shows an established prophet is trusted without a sign.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so (introduces a proof)
Where אליהו faced the prophets of בעל
Offerings slaughtered outside the בית המקדש, normally forbidden

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
Abraham at Mount Moriah,
how did Isaac listen to him?
Elijah at Mount Carmel,
how did they rely on him
and do slaughtering outside?
phrases.notes: Bringing an offering outside the בית המקדש is normally forbidden. They did it only because אליהו told them to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the distinction of Step 15 by showing what would go wrong without it.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that an established prophet needs no sign.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יצחק obeying אברהם at the עקידה, and the people following אליהו in bringing שחוטי חוץ at הר הכרמל.

steps.title: Conclusion: an established prophet is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats its conclusion: a prophet who is מוחזק does not need a sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, where he is established, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the proof by repeating the rule from Step 15, now shown to be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are the same as Step 15, but now they are a proven conclusion. The stories of אברהם and אליהו only make sense if an established prophet is trusted without a sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, so it must be (introduces the forced conclusion)

steps.whatToRemember: A listener is punished for ignoring a נביא if the נביא gave an אות. If the נביא is already מוחזק as a true prophet, no sign is needed.

phrases.english: Rather, where he is established, it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the conclusion forced by the proof in Step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An established prophet (מוחזק) must be obeyed even without a sign.

steps.title: After what events did God test אברהם?
steps.stepSummary: Starting a new topic connected to the עקידה, the גמרא quotes the פסוק 'after these matters, God tested אברהם' and asks: after what?
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'It was after these matters that God tested אברהם.' After what?
steps.whatsHappening: Since אברהם at הר המוריה was just mentioned, the גמרא opens a new discussion about the עקידה. This step sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the test came 'after these matters,' which suggests a link to something that happened earlier. The גמרא asks which earlier events led to the test.

keyTerms.meaning: After these matters (the opening words of the עקידה)

phrases.english: "And it was after these matters
that God tested Abraham":
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:1

phrases.english: After what?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיְהִי אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וְהָאֱלֹהִים נִסָּה אֶת אַבְרָהָם, אַחַר מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the mention of אברהם at הר המוריה in Step 16 to begin a new discussion about the עקידה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier events the words 'after these matters' refer to.

steps.title: After the words of the שטן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יוסי בן זימרא, explains that 'after these matters' means after the words of the שטן, which were spoken at יצחק's weaning feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי בן זימרא: it means after the words of the שטן, as it says 'And the child grew and was weaned, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18: what were the 'matters' that came before the test? The answer is the words of the שטן, said at the feast for יצחק's weaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דברים' in the פסוק can mean 'words' as well as 'matters'. רבי יוסי בן זימרא reads it as words someone spoke, and he links them to the feast in the earlier פסוק. The next steps tell us what those words were.

keyTerms.meaning: The accuser, the angel who speaks against people before ה׳

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra:
After the words of the Satan,
as it is written: "And the child grew and was weaned, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 21:8. The rest of that פסוק says אברהם made a big feast on the day יצחק was weaned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'after what?' from step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After the words of the שטן at יצחק's weaning feast.

steps.title: The שטן complains about אברהם's feast
steps.stepSummary: The שטן tells ה׳ that אברהם received a son at one hundred, yet at his whole feast he did not offer even one small bird to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שטן said before ה׳: Master of the World, You gave this old man a child at a hundred years old. Out of that whole feast, couldn't he spare one turtledove or one young pigeon to offer to You?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells us what the שטן's words actually were. He accuses אברהם of not thanking ה׳ with a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The complaint is that אברהם spent a lot on a party but gave nothing to ה׳. A turtledove or young pigeon is the cheapest קרבן there is, so the שטן is saying that אברהם could not spare even that.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of the womb, meaning a child
Turtledove, a bird used for a קרבן
Young pigeon, also used for a קרבן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שָׂטָן לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The Satan said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
this old man, You graciously granted him
at a hundred years old, a fruit of the womb,
out of the entire feast that he made,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה לוֹ תּוֹר אֶחָד אוֹ גּוֹזָל אֶחָד
phrases.english: did he not have one turtledove or one young pigeon
to offer before You?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר שטן לפני הקדוש ברוך הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the content of the 'words of the שטן' mentioned in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן accused אברהם of making a great feast without offering any קרבן to ה׳.

steps.title: ה׳ answers, and the test begins
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ replies that the feast was only in honor of his son, and that אברהם would even slaughter that son if commanded. Right away, ה׳ tested אברהם.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ said to him: Did he make the feast for any reason other than his son? If I tell him 'Slaughter your son before Me,' he will slaughter him right away. Right away, 'And God tested אברהם.'
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ defends אברהם against the שטן. The גמרא says this conversation is what led straight to the עקידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳'s point is that the feast was about joy over the child, not about holding back from ה׳‎. אברהם's loyalty is so complete that he would give up the child himself. The test of the עקידה then shows openly that ה׳ was right.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it asks: 'Did he do anything at all except...?'

steps.whatToRemember: According to this מימרא, the עקידה happened because of the שטן's complaint. Its purpose was to show that אברהם would give ה׳ even his beloved son.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Did he make it for anything other than for his son?
If I say to him,
"Slaughter your son before Me,"
he would slaughter him immediately.
Immediately, "And God tested Abraham."
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:1.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: ה׳'s reply to the שטן's complaint in step 20, which leads to the test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ defended אברהם, and the test of the עקידה followed immediately.

steps.title: The word נא means 'please'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'Take, please, your son', and רבי שמעון בר אבא explains that 'נא' is a word of request, not a command.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And He said: Take, please, your son.' רבי שמעון בר אבא said: 'נא' always means a request.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק of the עקידה and points out one word in it. ה׳ asked אברהם with 'please' instead of simply commanding him. This sets up the משל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ is the King and could simply give an order, so the word 'please' is surprising. רבי שמעון בר אבא tells us to read it as a real request. The משל that follows explains why ה׳ would ask.

phrases.english: "And He said: Take, please, your son."
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:2.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon bar Abba said:
"Na" is nothing but an expression of request.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the עקידה story with the next פסוק and focuses on one word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'נא' means 'please', a request rather than a command.

steps.title: A משל of a king and his warrior
steps.stepSummary: A king won many wars through one warrior. When a fierce war came, he asked the warrior, 'please stand for me', so people would not say the earlier victories meant nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A משל: a human king faced many wars, and he had one warrior who won them all. Later a very hard war came. The king said to him: Please, stand for me in this war, so people won't say the earlier wins had no real substance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בר אבא gives a משל to explain why ה׳ said 'please'. This step tells the story; the next step applies it to אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king does not doubt his warrior. He asks because one loss in the biggest war would make everyone say the earlier victories were luck or meant nothing. The request comes from wanting to protect the warrior's earlier achievements.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh and blood, meaning a human being

phrases.english: A parable of a king of flesh and blood
against whom many wars rose up,
and he had one warrior, and he defeated them.
After some time, a fierce war rose up against him.
He said to him: I request of you,
stand for me in this war,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת אֵין בָּהֶם מַמָּשׁ.
phrases.english: so that they will not say the first ones had no substance.
phrases.notes: 'The first ones' means the earlier victories.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a משל to explain the 'please' of step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king asks his proven warrior, 'please', to win one last hard battle so the earlier victories are not dismissed.

steps.title: Applying the משל to אברהם
steps.stepSummary: In the same way, ה׳ told אברהם: I tested you many times and you passed. Please pass this test too, so people won't say the earlier tests meant nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, ה׳ said to אברהם: I tested you with several tests and you passed them all. Now please stand for Me in this test, so people won't say the earlier ones had no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the משל. אברהם is the warrior, his earlier tests are the earlier wars, and the עקידה is the fierce final war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we see why ה׳ said 'please'. The עקידה was the hardest test, and failing it would make people doubt all of אברהם's earlier tests. ה׳ was asking, not doubting.
steps.whatToRemember: 'נא' means 'please'. ה׳ asked אברהם to pass the hardest test so that his earlier tests would keep their full value.

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר לְאַבְרָהָם:
phrases.english: So too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Abraham:
I have tested you with several tests
and you withstood them all.
Now stand for Me in this test,
so that they will not say there was no substance in the first ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אף הקדוש ברוך הוא אמר לאברהם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משל of step 23 to ה׳ and אברהם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ asked אברהם to pass the עקידה so that his earlier tests would not be dismissed.

steps.title: Your son, your only one, whom you love, יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the פסוק as a conversation. After each description ה׳ gives, אברהם answers that it could fit both his sons, until ה׳ names יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Your son.' I have two sons. 'Your only one.' Each one is the only son of his mother. 'Whom you love.' I love both of them. 'יצחק.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק uses four descriptions instead of just saying 'יצחק'. It reads it as ה׳ speaking and אברהם replying each time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each description could fit both ישמעאל and יצחק. 'Your son' fits both, and 'your only one' fits both, since each was the only son of his own mother. 'Whom you love' fits both too, so only the name 'יצחק' makes it clear.

phrases.english: "Your son."
phrases.notes: Here ה׳ is speaking, and the next line is אברהם's reply. The גמרא doesn't say who is talking, so read it as a back-and-forth.

phrases.english: I have two sons.
"Your only one."

phrases.aramaic: זֶה יָחִיד לְאִמּוֹ וְזֶה יָחִיד לְאִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: This one is an only son to his mother, and that one is an only son to his mother.
"Whom you love."
I love both of them.
"Isaac."

steps.triggerLanguage: את בנך שני בנים יש לי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק (בראשית 22:2), now looking at its four descriptions of the son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ revealed which son He meant step by step, and named יצחק only at the end.

steps.title: Why the long buildup?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ה׳ used so many steps instead of naming יצחק right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all of this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ה׳ stretched out the command. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ could have said 'take יצחק' at the start. The question is what purpose the slow buildup served.

phrases.english: And why all of this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the long conversation in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why ה׳ did not name יצחק immediately.

steps.title: So אברהם would not be overwhelmed
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ built up slowly so that אברהם's mind would not be thrown into shock by the sudden command.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that his mind would not be overwhelmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the slow buildup was meant to protect אברהם from sudden shock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing 'slaughter יצחק' all at once could have overwhelmed אברהם. Revealing it bit by bit let him take in the news gradually.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind becomes overwhelmed or confused

phrases.english: So that his mind would not be thrown into confusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To keep אברהם from sudden shock, ה׳ revealed the command gradually.

steps.title: The שטן meets אברהם on the road
steps.stepSummary: The שטן goes ahead of אברהם on the way to the עקידה and uses פסוקים from איוב to suggest that he is now weakening.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שטן got ahead of him on the road and said: 'If someone tests you with a word, will you grow weary?... You taught many and strengthened weak hands. Your words lifted up those who stumbled... But now it comes to you, and you grow weary.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new scene begins: the שטן tries to stop אברהם on the way. He uses words from איוב to suggest that אברהם, who encouraged others, is now failing himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטן's argument is: you comforted and strengthened many people, but now that the hardship is yours, you are breaking. He is trying to plant doubt and regret in אברהם.

keyTerms.meaning: He went ahead of him, intercepted him

phrases.english: The Satan went ahead of him on the road.
He said to him:
"If one tries a word with you, will you be weary?...
phrases.notes: איוב 4:2–5. The dots mean the גמרא skips some words of the פסוקים.

phrases.english: Behold, you have instructed many,
and you strengthened weak hands.
Your words lifted up the one who stumbles...
But now it comes to you, and you are weary."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story ahead to אברהם's journey to the עקידה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן tried to weaken אברהם on the road by suggesting he was failing his own test.

steps.title: אברהם answers: I will walk with my integrity
steps.stepSummary: אברהם answers the שטן with a פסוק: 'I will walk in my wholeheartedness.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'I will walk in my wholeheartedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם does not argue with the שטן. He answers with a פסוק saying he will keep going with complete loyalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטן tried to stir up doubt, and אברהם answers only with his commitment. 'Wholeheartedness' means serving ה׳ fully, without second-guessing.

phrases.english: He said to him:
"I will walk in my wholeheartedness."
phrases.notes: תהלים 26:11.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אברהם's reply to the שטן's words in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אברהם rejects the שטן's doubts and keeps walking with full loyalty.

steps.title: The שטן calls אברהם's fear of ה׳ foolishness
steps.stepSummary: The שטן keeps going and quotes איוב again, mocking אברהם: your fear of ה׳ is really your foolishness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שטן said to him: 'Is not your fear of God your foolishness?'
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם just answered the שטן, and now the שטן tries again with another פסוק from איוב. He is mocking אברהם for following ה׳'s command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטן's claim is that אברהם's יראת שמים is about to lead him to something foolish: killing his own son. It is a direct attack on the value of serving ה׳ when the command seems to make no sense.

phrases.english: He said to him: "Is not your fear [of God] your foolishness?"
phrases.notes: The שטן is speaking. איוב 4:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The שטן renews his attack after אברהם's answer in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן says that אברהם's fear of ה׳ is foolishness, since it will lead him to kill his son.

steps.title: אברהם answers that no innocent person is lost
steps.stepSummary: אברהם answers with the next פסוק in איוב: remember, who that was innocent ever perished?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Remember, please, who that was innocent ever perished?'
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם pushes back, using the very next פסוק in the same place in איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם trusts that ה׳ is fair. Someone who follows ה׳ with a clean heart will not lose out, so his יראה is not foolish.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״זְכׇר נָא מִי הוּא נָקִי אָבָד״.
phrases.english: He said to him: "Remember, please, who that was innocent ever perished?"
phrases.notes: Now אברהם is speaking. איוב 4:7

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: זְכׇר נָא מִי הוּא נָקִי אָבָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שטן's mockery from step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is fearing ה׳ foolish when it seems to lead to disaster?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. ה׳ does not let the innocent be lost.

steps.title: The שטן claims he heard from heaven that יצחק will not be sacrificed
steps.stepSummary: Since אברהם is not listening, the שטן switches tactics. He says he overheard in heaven that the sheep is the offering, not יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he saw that אברהם was not listening to him, he said: 'A word was secretly brought to me.' This is what I heard from behind the heavenly curtain: the sheep is for the burnt offering, and יצחק is not for the burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: Arguing has failed, so the שטן now claims to have inside information from heaven. He hopes it will get אברהם to stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the שטן said the command was foolish. Now he says the command is not real at all: heaven has already decided that a sheep, not יצחק, will be the offering. This is a sneakier attack because it sounds like a holy message.

keyTerms.meaning: Was brought secretly, was 'stolen' to me
The heavenly curtain, behind which heavenly decisions are heard

steps.confusionAlert: Do not be surprised that a ram really was offered in the end. The שטן's claim turns out to be true, and that is exactly the point of אברהם's answer in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזָא דְּלָא קָא שָׁמַיע לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Once he saw that he was not listening to him,
he said to him: "Now a word was secretly brought to me."
phrases.notes: איוב 4:12

phrases.english: This is what I heard from behind the curtain:
"The sheep is for a burnt offering," and יצחק is not for a burnt offering.
phrases.notes: He twists words from בראשית 22:8, where אברהם says ה׳ will provide the sheep.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזָא דְּלָא קָא שָׁמַיע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After being rejected in step 31, the שטן tries a new tactic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן claims a heavenly message that יצחק will not be the offering.

steps.title: A liar is not believed even when he tells the truth
steps.stepSummary: אברהם answers that a liar is punished by not being believed, even when he says something true.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is the punishment of a liar: even when he says the truth, people do not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם closes the story by refusing to trust the שטן at all, and he keeps going with the עקידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם does not argue about whether the claim is true. He rejects the speaker himself: a known liar loses his believability. So even real information from the שטן cannot stop אברהם from doing ה׳'s command.

keyTerms.meaning: A liar, someone who makes things up

steps.whatToRemember: The שטן tried three ways to stop אברהם: weakness, foolishness, and a claimed 'inside report' from heaven. אברהם answered each one, and the last one by refusing to believe a liar even if he speaks truth.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כָּךְ עוֹנְשׁוֹ שֶׁל בַּדַּאי,
phrases.english: He said to him: This is the punishment of a liar,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אָמַר אֱמֶת אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ.
phrases.english: that even if he says the truth, people do not listen to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: כָּךְ עוֹנְשׁוֹ שֶׁל בַּדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the שטן's claim from step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Should אברהם stop because of the שטן's 'heavenly report'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. A liar is not believed even when he speaks the truth.

steps.title: רבי לוי: the test came after ישמעאל boasted to יצחק
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי gives a different meaning for 'after these things': it means after ישמעאל boasted that his מילה at thirteen was greater than יצחק's at eight days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: 'After these things' means after the words of ישמעאל to יצחק. ישמעאל said to יצחק: I am greater than you in מצוות, because you had your מילה at eight days old, and I had mine at thirteen years old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a new explanation of the opening words of the עקידה story, 'after these things.' רבי לוי says they point to an argument between ישמעאל and יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the 'things' were linked to the שטן's complaints. רבי לוי links them to ישמעאל's boast instead. ישמעאל's claim is that a מצוה done as an adult, by choice, is worth more than one done to a baby.

keyTerms.meaning: After his words, explaining 'after these things'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי לֵוִי אָמַר: אַחַר דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל יִשְׁמָעֵאל לְיִצְחָק.
phrases.english: רבי לוי says: After the words of ישמעאל to יצחק.
ישמעאל said to יצחק:
I am greater than you in מצוות,
for you were circumcised at eight days old,
and I at thirteen years old.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי לֵוִי אָמַר: אַחַר דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל יִשְׁמָעֵאל לְיִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of 'after these things' from the one connected to the שטן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'After these things' refers to ישמעאל's boast to יצחק about his מילה.

steps.title: יצחק answers that he would give his whole self, and the test follows
steps.stepSummary: יצחק answers that he would give his whole life if ה׳ asked. Right away ה׳ tested אברהם.
steps.simpleTranslation: יצחק said to him: You are trying to impress me with one body part? If ה׳ told me, 'Sacrifice yourself before Me,' I would sacrifice myself. Right away: 'And God tested אברהם.'
steps.whatsHappening: יצחק answers ישמעאל's boast. The גמרא then shows that the עקידה came right after his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישמעאל gave one body part. יצחק says he is ready to give his whole life. The עקידה follows 'immediately,' which shows it was the chance to make יצחק's words real.

keyTerms.meaning: Provoke, try to show off against

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי לוי, the עקידה was set off by יצחק's own offer to give his life for ה׳.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וּבְאֵבֶר אֶחָד אַתָּה מְגָרֶה בִּי?
phrases.english: He said to him: And with one body part you provoke me?

phrases.aramaic: אִם אוֹמֵר לִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: If the Holy One, Blessed be He, would say to me
"Sacrifice yourself before Me," I would sacrifice [myself].
Immediately: "And God tested Abraham."
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:1

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וּבְאֵבֶר אֶחָד אַתָּה מְגָרֶה בִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: יצחק answers ישמעאל's boast from step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is ישמעאל really greater because he chose his מילה as an adult?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. יצחק would give his entire life, and the עקידה came right away to test it.

steps.title: How a נביא who leads people astray, and those who lead a city astray, are put to death
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a נביא who leads people to עבודה זרה gets סקילה, and רבי שמעון says חנק. The same argument applies to those who lead an עיר הנדחת astray.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: A נביא who led people astray is put to death by stoning. רבי שמעון says: by strangling. Those who lead a city astray so it becomes an עיר הנדחת are put to death by stoning. רבי שמעון says: by strangling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the stories and goes back to הלכה. It brings a ברייתא about which death penalty applies to people who lead others to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases are listed: a נביא who pushes people to worship idols, and people who lead a whole city to worship idols. In both, the חכמים say סקילה, the harsher death, and רבי שמעון says חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: A prophet who leads people astray to עבודה זרה
Those who lead a city astray so it becomes an idolatrous city

phrases.english: The Sages taught: A prophet who led astray – by stoning.
Rabbi Shimon says: By strangling.
Those who lead astray an idolatrous city – by stoning.
Rabbi Shimon says: By strangling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and opens a new הלכה topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: a נביא שהדיח and מדיחי עיר הנדחת get סקילה. רבי שמעון: חנק.

steps.title: What is the source of the חכמים for stoning a נביא שהדיח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the first ruling and asks for the reason of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A נביא who led astray gets stoning.' What is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first line of the ברייתא again so it can ask where the חכמים learn that the punishment is סקילה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives a death penalty for a נביא שהדיח but does not clearly say which kind. So the גמרא wants to know how the חכמים know it is סקילה.

phrases.english: A prophet who led astray – by stoning.
What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the חכמים' ruling in step 36.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that a נביא שהדיח gets סקילה.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from מסית: 'leading astray' and 'leading astray'
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים learn from the word הדחה, which appears both by a נביא and by a מסית. Just as a מסית gets סקילה, so does the נביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it through the word 'leading astray' here and 'leading astray' by a מסית. Just as there the punishment is stoning, so too here it is stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה: the same word is used in both places, so the law of one is applied to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה clearly says a מסית, a regular person who pushes someone to עבודה זרה, gets סקילה. The word הדחה appears in both sections, so the חכמים carry סקילה over to the נביא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from (a גזירה שוה)
A regular person who pushes someone to worship idols
Just as there, so too here

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a גזירה שוה works: one shared word lets a clear law from one case fill in a missing detail in another.

phrases.english: It is derived from "leading astray" here and "leading astray" by an instigator:
phrases.notes: The same word appears in both sections of דברים 13, which is what links the two cases.

phrases.english: Just as there it is by stoning,
so too here it is by stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Source for סקילה for a נביא שהדיח.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of הדחה–הדחה from מסית, who gets סקילה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reason: an unspecified death means strangulation
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that a נביא who leads people astray (נביא שהדיח) gets חנק. The Torah only says 'he shall die' about him, and any death the Torah does not describe is חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? The Torah writes 'death' about the נביא, and every death the Torah mentions without saying which kind is only חנק.
steps.whatsHappening: The last step gave the חכמים' reason for סקילה. Now the גמרא gives רבי שמעון's reason for saying the נביא gets חנק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not use the הדחה comparison to the מסית. He goes by the plain wording, which simply says the נביא 'shall die.' He then applies the general rule that a death the Torah does not spell out is the mildest kind, חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: Death; here, the Torah's plain wording that the person shall die
Without detail; not saying which kind
Strangulation, one of the four court executions

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that an unspecified death means חנק is a general principle used all over ש״ס, not only here.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking: what is רבי שמעון's reason?

phrases.english: death is written about him,
phrases.notes: דברים 13:6, 'that prophet shall be put to death.'

phrases.english: and every death stated in the Torah without detail
is nothing other than strangulation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the מחלוקת, after the חכמים' source in step 38
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse says only 'death' about the נביא, and any unspecified death in the Torah is חנק

steps.title: What is the חכמים' source that city inciters are stoned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second ruling of the ברייתא: the people who lead a city to עבודה זרה get סקילה. It asks for the חכמים' source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those who lead a city astray so it becomes an עיר הנדחת get סקילה. What is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second half of the ברייתא and asks for the חכמים' source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the same מחלוקת applies to the מדיחי עיר הנדחת: the חכמים say סקילה and רבי שמעון says חנק. The גמרא now wants the source for this case, just as it did for the נביא.

keyTerms.meaning: The people who lead a whole city into עבודה זרה
A city whose people were led astray to worship idols
Stoning, the most severe of the court executions

phrases.english: Those who lead a city astray are stoned,
what is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the נביא case, moves to the second case of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for giving סקילה to the מדיחי עיר הנדחת

steps.title: The חכמים learn from the word הדחה, from a מסית or a נביא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים learn from the word הדחה, which appears with the city inciters, the מסית and the נביא. Since both the מסית and (for them) the נביא get סקילה, the city inciters get סקילה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn 'הדחה' from 'הדחה,' either from the מסית or from the נביא who led others astray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים use a גזירה שוה on the word הדחה. They can learn it from either source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים it does not matter which source is used. Both the מסית and the נביא get סקילה in their view, so either comparison gives סקילה for the city inciters.

keyTerms.meaning: Leading astray; the shared word used for the comparison
A regular person who persuades someone to worship idols
A prophet who led people astray

phrases.english: They learn 'incitement' from 'incitement,'
phrases.notes: The same word appears in the Torah's sections about each of these cases, so they are compared.

phrases.english: either from the instigator,
or from the prophet who incited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 40
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of הדחה from either the מסית or the נביא, both of whom get סקילה according to the חכמים

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns only from the prophet
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון also uses the הדחה comparison, but he learns it from the נביא. For him the נביא gets חנק, so the city inciters get חנק too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון learns 'הדחה' from 'הדחה' from the נביא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי שמעון reaches חנק for the city inciters. He compares them to the נביא, who gets חנק in his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides use the same tool, a comparison through the word הדחה. They disagree about the source: רבי שמעון picks the נביא, and that choice is what makes his answer חנק.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon learns
'incitement' from 'incitement' from the prophet.
phrases.notes: Since רבי שמעון gives the נביא חנק (step 39), the city inciters get חנק as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן גָּמַר הַדָּחָה הַדָּחָה מִנָּבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's version of the comparison
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון learns the city inciters' punishment from the נביא, so they get חנק

steps.title: Why not learn from the regular instigator?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: why not compare the city inciters to the regular מסית? That source gives סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him learn it from the מסית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's choice of source. Why the נביא and not the מסית?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The city inciters are regular people, not prophets, so they seem closer to the regular מסית. If רבי שמעון learned from the מסית, he would end up with סקילה like the חכמים.

phrases.english: But let him learn from the instigator!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source chosen in step 42
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's choice to compare the city inciters to the נביא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The city inciters are ordinary people like the מסית, so the מסית seems the better source, and it would give סקילה

steps.title: Leading many is compared to leading many
steps.stepSummary: Those who lead a whole city astray are leading many people, and so does a נביא. A regular מסית usually entices only one person. So רבי שמעון compares many to many.
steps.simpleTranslation: We compare one who leads many astray to one who leads many astray. We do not compare one who leads many astray to one who leads a single person astray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון. The נביא is the better match because, like the city inciters, he leads many people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key feature here is how many people are led astray, not whether the person is a prophet. The city inciters and the נביא both work on a crowd, while the מסית works on one person.

keyTerms.meaning: We compare and learn one case from another
One who leads many people astray
One who leads a single person astray

phrases.english: We learn one who leads many astray from one who leads many astray,
phrases.notes: The 'many' on both sides are the city inciters and the נביא, who speaks to the public.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דָּנִין מֵסִית רַבִּים מִמֵּסִית יָחִיד.
phrases.english: and we do not learn one who leads many astray from one who leads an individual astray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 43
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a closer similarity: leading many people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The city inciters should be compared to the regular מסית because both are ordinary people
steps.terutzMaskana: They are compared to the נביא because both lead many people astray

steps.title: On the contrary, compare an ordinary person to an ordinary person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the better match may be ordinary person to ordinary person. The city inciters are not prophets, so they should not be learned from a נביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! We compare a regular person to a regular person, and we do not compare a regular person to a נביא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It suggests a different feature that should decide which source to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer focused on how many people were led astray. This challenge focuses on who the inciter is. The city inciters are ordinary people like the מסית, and being a נביא is a big difference that could change the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; it is the other way around
An ordinary person, not a prophet

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two features. Step 44 matches cases by how MANY people were led astray. This step matches them by WHO did the leading, an ordinary person or a נביא.

phrases.english: On the contrary, we learn an ordinary person from an ordinary person,
and we do not learn an ordinary person from a prophet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 44 with a competing comparison
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the city inciters should be compared to the נביא because both lead many
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The city inciters are ordinary people, so the ordinary מסית is the closer match, and that points to סקילה

steps.title: A prophet who leads people astray becomes an ordinary person
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that once a נביא leads people to עבודה זרה, he loses his special status and is the most ordinary person there is. So the city inciters, who are ordinary people, can be compared to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון holds: once he has led people astray, you have no one more ordinary than this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 45 for רבי שמעון. It explains why ordinary city inciters can still be learned from a נביא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that the city inciters are ordinary people, while a נביא is special, so they don't match. The answer is that a נביא who leads people astray throws away his special standing and becomes a plain הדיוט. So the match is ordinary person to ordinary person after all, and רבי שמעון can learn חנק from the נביא.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person, someone with no special status
He led people astray, especially toward עבודה זרה
There is no one, you won't find anyone

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the city inciters get חנק like the נביא. Both lead many people astray, and a נביא who does this becomes an ordinary person, so the comparison holds both ways.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the נביא was never a prophet. It says that by leading people astray he lowered himself, and for this law he is treated like an ordinary person.

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון holds:
once he has led people astray,
phrases.notes: "He" is the נביא from step 45, who led people to worship idols.

phrases.english: you have no greater ordinary person than this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 45, which said ordinary city inciters should not be learned from a נביא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the status of one side of the comparison: the inciting נביא counts as an ordinary person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נביא is special, so ordinary city inciters can't be learned from him.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נביא who leads people astray becomes the most ordinary person of all, so the comparison to the city inciters stands, and they get חנק.

steps.title: Introducing a new statement from רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a teaching from רב חסדא. The teaching itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setup. The גמרא is about to quote רב חסדא, but his actual words appear at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far this line only tells us who is speaking. The next amud shows what רב חסדא teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from בבל, a student of רב
Said, says. It introduces a teaching

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the רבי שמעון discussion to a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. Only the speaker's name appears here.
